microtheory.name: slang_lexis
microtheory.definition: How non-standard, in-group, expressive vocabulary is STORED and ACCESSED. Synthesised from: SlangNet (Dhuliawala et al. 2016, LREC) — a WordNet-like resource where slang senses are grouped into synsets, each linked to the STANDARD sense it diverges from, so a slang form can be distinguished from its conventional reading; the slang-generation framework (Sun, Zhang + Xu 2021, TACL) — slang 'encodes novel slang meaning by RELATING the conventional and slang senses of a word', choosing a form by probabilistic inference (semantic PROXIMITY to existing senses) plus CONTRAST (expressive distance); and the sociolinguistic core — slang's defining function is SOCIAL INDEXING: it signals membership of an in-group / persona. Substrate analogue: a slang term is a surface FORM bound by an edge to the standard Concept it denotes, tagged with the persona/register that owns it; comprehension follows the form->concept edge, production inverts it.

concepts.name: slang
concepts.definition: Informal, non-standard, often ephemeral vocabulary whose DEFINING function is social indexing — it marks the speaker as a member of an in-group/persona. A slang term is a surface FORM that denotes a standard Concept while differing from that Concept's canonical form. Substrate analogue: a variant FORM with a denotes-edge to a Concept and a persona tag.

concepts.name: lexical_variant
concepts.definition: An alternative surface FORM for a meaning: the triple (form, denoted-concept, register/persona). The standard form is one variant; slang/informal/technical forms are others. Storage unit for slang. Substrate analogue: a node carrying form + register, with a denotes-edge to its Concept.

concepts.name: denotation
concepts.definition: The conventional Concept a form maps to — the standard sense. Slang RELATES a form's slang sense to this conventional sense (Sun+Xu 2021). Substrate analogue: the denotes-edge from a variant form to its Concept.

concepts.name: variant_set
concepts.definition: Many forms, one meaning: the set of all variant forms denoting a single Concept (the SlangNet 'synset' idea). Lets a Concept be reached from any of its forms and any form be produced from the Concept. Substrate analogue: all variants sharing a denotes-edge to the same Concept.

concepts.name: social_indexing
concepts.definition: Slang's primary job: a form signals identity/affiliation. The persona a variant carries IS the group it indexes; recognising the persona's characteristic forms = recognising the persona. Substrate analogue: the persona attribute on a variant; the marker by which express_in_persona and persona-perception operate.

concepts.name: slang_comprehension
concepts.definition: DECODING: map an incoming slang FORM to the conventional Concept it denotes (follow form->denotes->concept). Mirrors standard referent-resolution but via the variant edge rather than form==name. Distinguishing the slang sense from the conventional one is the WSD task SlangNet targets. Substrate analogue: a resolution that wires Mention->refers_to->Concept when the Mention text matches a variant form.

concepts.name: slang_production
concepts.definition: ENCODING: given a Concept and a target persona/register, choose the variant FORM that denotes the Concept and carries that persona. The inverse of comprehension over the same (form, concept, persona) triple. This is the real work behind express_in_persona. Substrate analogue: Argmax/Filter over the Concept's variants by persona match.

concepts.name: proximity_extension
concepts.definition: One way new slang arises (Sun+Xu 2021): a form EXTENDS to a meaning that is semantically NEAR its existing senses — analogical, category-based. Predicts/learns which form a community will reuse for a new meaning. Substrate analogue: prefer binding an unresolved form to the Concept nearest its existing denotations.

concepts.name: contrastive_expressivity
concepts.definition: The other mechanism (Sun+Xu 2021): a form is chosen for expressive CONTRAST — distance, novelty, affect — not similarity. Slang is deliberately marked against the standard form to carry attitude/intensity. Substrate analogue: an affect/intensity tag on a variant; chosen when expressive load is wanted over neutrality.

concepts.name: ephemerality
concepts.definition: Slang is temporally and community-bound — forms rise, shift, and die; the same form indexes different groups across eras. Stored variants should carry era/community so access can weight by recency + community match. Substrate analogue: era/community attributes weighting comprehension + production.

concepts.name: oov_slang_signal
concepts.definition: An out-of-vocabulary token — a Mention matching no standard Concept name — is a CANDIDATE slang form to be learned, not noise. The under-representation of slang in standard lexica (Sun+Xu 2021) means OOV is the normal entry point for slang acquisition. Substrate analogue: an unresolved Mention is the trigger to learn a new variant (bind form->concept under the active persona).

concepts.name: slang_acquisition
concepts.definition: Learning a new slang form ON ONE'S OWN: DETECT an unresolved token (oov_slang_signal = a Mention with no refers_to after comprehension), CONFIRM it is slang and recover its meaning + owning persona (from a teacher or from context), then COIN a variant (form + denotes_name + persona) which the wiring faculty binds to the one canonical Concept. The slang lexicon GROWS from use; the agent itself notices what it does not know. Substrate analogue: an oov-detector Term over a Message + a grounding step + minting a SlangVariant.

concepts.name: persona_inference
concepts.definition: Recognising WHICH persona/in-group is speaking from the slang present — the converse of production. Each known variant carries the persona it indexes (social_indexing), so the personas of an utterance's KNOWN variants vote and the dominant one is the active persona. This both identifies the interlocutor's register AND lets a newly-coined slang form be attributed to the right persona BY THE AGENT ITSELF, with no outside declaration: if you recognise some of a group's slang you recognise the group, and you assign its new slang to it. Substrate analogue: Argmax over the personas of the variants the utterance's mentions resolved through (the via_variant edges).

concepts.name: meaning_inference
concepts.definition: Recovering an unknown word's MEANING from the company it keeps (Firth's distributional hypothesis: 'you shall know a word by the company it keeps'; the proximity mechanism of Sun+Xu 2021). Unlike a persona — a SHARED attribute the co-occurring known words can vote — meaning is particular to each word, so it is recovered not by voting but from STRUCTURAL FRAMES that equate or relate the unknown word to a KNOWN one in the same utterance: EQUATION/apposition ('X means/is Y', 'X, i.e. Y') gives the meaning EXACTLY (X denotes Y's concept); COORDINATION ('X and/or Y') gives it by PROXIMITY (X denotes a meaning near Y's). The agent reads the unknown token's adjacency (prev_mention/next_mention), and if a known resolved token sits across a connector, takes that concept as the unknown's meaning — grounding meaning ON ITS OWN when context carries a cue, and falling back to a teacher only when context is silent. Substrate analogue: a Term over the OOV mention's connector-gated neighbours -> the neighbour's refers_to Concept.

rules.name: slang_is_a_form_not_a_new_concept
rules.head: the substrate meets a slang word
rules.body: it stores the word as a surface FORM (a lexical_variant) bound by a denotes-edge to the STANDARD Concept it means, NOT as a brand-new Concept. Comprehension then follows form->denotes->concept instead of matching form==concept.name, so 'avast'/'sup'/'gnarly' resolve to greeting/quality just like their standard forms do.

rules.name: slang_carries_the_persona_that_owns_it
rules.head: the substrate stores or learns a slang variant
rules.body: it tags the variant with the persona/community that uses it, because slang's defining function is social_indexing. The set of a persona's characteristic variant forms IS its identity signature — the thing persona-perception detects and express_in_persona reproduces.

rules.name: slang_access_is_bidirectional_over_one_triple
rules.head: the substrate needs to understand or produce slang
rules.body: it uses ONE stored (form, concept, persona) triple two ways: COMPREHENSION reads form->concept (decode an incoming form), PRODUCTION reads concept+persona->form (encode a meaning in a persona's voice). They are inverses; storing the triple once enables both.

rules.name: many_forms_one_meaning_group_as_a_variant_set
rules.head: the substrate holds several slang forms denoting the same Concept
rules.body: it groups them as a variant_set under that Concept (the SlangNet synset). The Concept is reachable from any of its forms; any form is producible from the Concept; comprehension is robust to which form appears.

rules.name: new_slang_arises_by_proximity_or_contrast
rules.head: the substrate must coin or learn a slang form for a meaning
rules.body: it accounts for two mechanisms: PROXIMITY (reuse a form whose existing senses are semantically near the new meaning — analogical) and CONTRAST (pick a form that is expressively distant/novel to carry affect). A learned variant records which mechanism produced it.

rules.name: unresolved_tokens_are_candidate_slang
rules.head: the substrate sees a Mention that matches no standard Concept name
rules.body: it treats the token as a candidate slang form to LEARN, not as noise: bind the new form to its intended Concept (from context or a teacher) under the active persona. This is the normal path because slang is under-represented in standard vocabulary.

rules.name: weight_access_by_recency_and_community
rules.head: the substrate accesses a slang variant
rules.body: it weights by ephemerality — prefer variants whose era is recent and whose community/persona matches the active context — because the same form indexes different groups across time and group.

rules.name: confirm_then_coin_oov_slang
rules.head: the substrate meets an unresolved token (a Mention with no refers_to after comprehension)
rules.body: it does NOT assume noise and it does NOT assume slang: it first CONFIRMS whether the token is slang and recovers its meaning + owning persona (asking a teacher, or inferring from context/proximity to the resolved concepts around it). ONLY on confirmation does it COIN a variant (form, denotes_name, persona); a merely-unknown ordinary word is left to normal word-learning. Coining once is enough — the wiring faculty binds the new variant to the canonical Concept and the next encounter resolves.

rules.name: infer_persona_from_co_occurring_slang
rules.head: the substrate must attribute a newly-coined slang form to a persona
rules.body: it INFERS the owning persona from the utterance ITSELF rather than taking an outside declaration: the personas of the KNOWN slang variants co-occurring in the same utterance vote, and the dominant one is the active persona (slang indexes the group; recognising some of a group's slang recognises the group). The new form is attributed to that inferred persona. It falls back to 'general' only when no known slang anchors the utterance. The meaning may still come from a teacher; the PERSONA the agent works out on its own.

rules.name: infer_meaning_from_context_before_asking
rules.head: the substrate must ground the MEANING of an unknown word
rules.body: it first tries to read the meaning from the company the word keeps (meaning_inference): a known resolved word equated with it ('X means/is Y', apposition) gives the meaning exactly; a known resolved word coordinated with it ('X and/or Y') gives it by proximity. Meaning is per-word, so it is taken from such a STRUCTURAL frame, not voted like a persona. ONLY when the context carries no such cue does the substrate fall back to asking a teacher. Thus the agent grounds both meaning and persona on its own whenever the surrounding language supports it.
